profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Denver, Colorado, tagged telecom=data_center, is named Pearl Plaza Office Building. As the name plainly states, this is a general-purpose commercial office building, the kind of property that houses multiple business tenants across floors of leased office space, not a purpose-built or converted data center. Office buildings frequently contain a telecommunications equipment room or meet-me room used to bring internet and phone service into the building for its tenants, and it is common for OpenStreetMap contributors mapping such rooms, or simply the building's main utility or IT closet, to apply the same telecom=data_center tag used for genuine wholesale and retail colocation facilities. That tagging pattern, rather than an undisclosed data center business operating inside an office tower, is the far more plausible explanation here. No data-center-specific operational detail, capacity, or specification is offered for this record because none is applicable to an office building; this entry exists to document the mistag honestly rather than to manufacture facility specifications for a site that is not, in fact, a data center.
profile.research_note: Pearl Plaza Office Building, tagged telecom=data_center in downtown Denver, is a named office building rather than a data center by its own OSM name. Downtown Denver office towers commonly house telecom equipment rooms or a tenant's IT closet, which is likely the source of this mistag rather than the building functioning as a colocation or cloud facility.
sources_tried: Nominatim reverse geocode at the stored coordinates returns "Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology, 601 East 18th Avenue, Denver CO", a state-government building, not a business named Pearl Plaza; the mismatch could not be resolved to a private operator

reading.body:
This record cannot be read as a data center campus. The facility is registered at coordinates that reverse-geocode to a Colorado state government building, not a commercial data center operator. The operator field is blank because research identified no private operator to attribute to the name "Pearl Plaza Office Building," and registry policy prohibits guessing at an entity from a generic name alone.

The mismatch between the registered name and the address suggests either a data entry error in this registry or a misidentification of what occupies the location. Without a website, a confirmed operator, or published specifications for IT load, power capacity, or grid connection, this entry holds no information about AI infrastructure.

Colorado has 17 mapped facilities across the state, of which only 3 publish capacity figures totaling 26.35 MW. This record contributes neither a resolved operator nor a published megawatt figure to that state total. It remains an open research item pending manual review or a search tool capable of disambiguating the actual tenant or operator at this address.
